title: Explanation soundness check
summary: Whether the explanation is sound: the question it answers and its boundary, a claim map with each claim marked sourced, common knowledge, opinion or unsupported, a trace of factual claims to the linked sources, a reasoning check, an explain-back by a reader using the text alone, and a type check for instructions and reference tables. A subject expert confirms flagged factual claims when no source supports them.
notAssessed: Whether the author's opinions are right: the check is that opinion is marked as opinion.
Claims about systems or history that no linked source covers, until the subject expert confirms them.
notes: Opinion and perspective belong in explanation; flagged only when presented as fact.
The subject expert checkpoint opens only when the trace flags claims; otherwise the author accepts or dismisses each finding.
Offer flagged instructional passages to Restructure to type as the seed of a how-to guide or reference.

config.instructions: Take the question the piece answers and the boundary it draws from the title and opening.

fields.name: question
fields.label: Question
fields.description: The why or about question the piece answers

fields.name: in_scope
fields.label: In scope
fields.description: What the piece says it covers

fields.name: out_of_scope
fields.label: Out of scope
fields.description: What the piece says it leaves to other pages

config.instructions: List each substantive claim (facts, history, reasons for decisions, comparisons, judgments) and how the text supports it.

fields.name: depends_on
fields.label: Depends on
fields.description: Earlier claims this one rests on, if any

config.question: Do the linked sources support this claim as stated? Opinion marked as opinion passes as stated_opinion; mark contradicted when a source says otherwise.

checklist.label: Bounded topic
checklist.question: Does the piece state the question it answers and keep to that boundary?

checklist.label: Conclusions follow
checklist.question: Do the conclusions follow from the claims made? Name any step that does not.

checklist.label: Alternatives and trade-offs
checklist.question: Are alternatives and trade-offs considered for the main decisions, rather than one design defended alone?

checklist.label: Opinion marked
checklist.question: Is opinion marked as opinion, rather than presented as fact?

checklist.label: History sourced
checklist.question: Are historical statements and dates attributed to a source rather than asserted from memory?

config.persona: an interested reader who knows the product's basics but not this topic, with only the text
config.task: Read the explanation once, then answer each question from the text alone, without outside knowledge.
rules: say "not answered" when the text does not give the answer
questions: What question does this piece answer, and where does its topic stop?
Why is the subject designed or done the way it is, according to the text?
What alternative was considered, and why was it not chosen?
What trade-off does the current approach accept?
How does this topic connect to a related concept the text mentions?

config.instructions: Classify each passage by its Diátaxis role in an explanation.

categories.label: Discussion
categories.description: Context, reasons, connections, alternatives or perspective

categories.label: Illustration
categories.description: An analogy, short example or diagram description that supports understanding

categories.label: Reference
categories.description: Option lists, parameter tables or facts to look up

config.instructions: Confirm or correct each flagged factual claim that no linked source supports. Leave out any you cannot judge.
